name: Joint Venture
beta: Reach the first bolted anchor, then work up and leftward along the corner, clipping bolts, finishing at a second anchor high on the wall.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Jules Verne
beta:
Launch from the T-2 start but dodge the old pegged crack; instead free the roof by borrowing T-2 handholds, then step left once over the lip. A slim, slanting roof comes next: tuck beneath it and pass it near its high end on the right.

Easy-angled 5.9 slab leads to a belay. Above, a thin flake bending right then left takes you up the vertical wall. Gear is hard to arrange here.
overview: A long, varied route that climbs the starting overhang using some holds shared with T-2, goes left to a narrow slanting roof, then follows a thin flake, a left-angling crack and later a vertical finger crack. Protection is hard to arrange.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: starts almost beside the beginning of T-2

name: Kansas Honey
beta:
The opening pitch is a steep, five-bolt slab ending beneath a conspicuous arch.

Next comes a bold leftward traverse with nothing to clip, around the arch and back right to a stance under the summit arch. A hand crack on the north side of that stance finishes the climb.
overview: A three-pitch Arch Rock route: a bolted slab to the first arch, an unprotected traverse around it, and a hand crack to the top.

current.area_walk_in: Several short, steep trails climb the slope to the base of the crag.

name: Kor's Korner
beta:
Start up some chopped footholds below a pointed buttress. The first pitch swings rightward around the buttress clipping old pitons, then enters a thin vertical crack where you jam the scars left by removed pins to a hanging stance.

Lowering off there is an option; otherwise head up and right via bolted-in pegs up to the top of the pillar. A modest rack of stoppers and small cams supplements the fixed gear.
overview: Two pitches: the first swings rightward around a sharp buttress past fixed pins into a vertical crack of pin scars, ending at a semi-hanging stance; the second moves up and rightward on drilled pegs, ending at the pillar's top. Also a clean C2 aid line.

current.anchor: semi-hanging stance in a shallow corner (lower-off point)
current.location: above the chopped steps beneath a sharp buttress

name: La Chaim
beta:
Either use a groove beside a neighbouring route or layback up the boulder's left flank and cut left. Climb a flake to its crest, then trace a pale dike to a blocky stance; the bottom is run out over easy face climbing with little protection.

The upper pitch is a lovely thin crack to the ledge where you walk off. Cams up to #2.5 are plenty.
overview: A sparsely protected start up a flake and white dike, then a gorgeous slim crack up to the exit ledge.

current.area_walk_in: Hike a little over a mile along the Black Canyon path, then pick up a cairned track leading to the base of the rock.
current.descent: walk off left along the ledge after two pitches
current.location: Groove directly west of the Neko’s Route start; or layback the boulder’s left edge and step across

name: Labor of Lust
beta: Start with a pair of flared parallel cracks to a bolted stance, then go up the rounded prow that sits to the left of Mariner. The upper part is a runout, serious lead.
overview: Four pitches on the rounded prow beside the Mariner slab: two flared cracks to a stance, sparsely protected friction on the arete, and a thin crack through the Sorcerer roof.

current.area_walk_in: Follow the Lumpy Ridge trail west past the old Twin Owls area, continue beyond the Book and the Bookmark, then take a faint spur to the southeast prow. A little scrambling is needed to get to the routes on the right.
current.location: Grass shelf where the approach slabs end, beneath the rounded arete that falls away left toward the Great Dihedral

name: Left Out
beta:
Begin on a block or flake on the slab's south side and wander up and to the left, clipping a handful of old quarter-inch bolts, up to a belay beneath the arch.

Then either rappel with two ropes or simply scramble to the top and walk down. Carry mid-size cams and large nuts to build the belay.

current.area_walk_in: A short walk from the road to the base; the wall rises straight up on the north side.
current.descent: rap 120 ft with two ropes, or walk off
current.location: begins on top of a flake or block at the slab's south side

name: Left Out (aka Lost Crack)
beta: Find the smooth slab beneath the Book's Isis Buttress and follow thin cracks (the crux) toward a faint dihedral right of centre. After that, ease leftward over simpler terrain, onto a series of ledges, and traverse them to the descent chimneys.
overview: The lone route on the rough eastern side of this crag: thin slab cracks to a faint corner, then easier ground to a ledge.

current.descent: traverse the ledge system left to the Bookmark Pinnacle descent chimneys
current.location: Smooth slab on the eastern side, beneath The Book’s Isis Buttress and a little west of it

name: Ellipse
beta:
Reach the base through an easy groove or chimney left of the lens. Begin in the gully by the low point: pull up and leftward over two bolts for the first hard moves, trace a seam till it fades, then finish on the beautiful rounded arete, which has another hard section by bolt four.

A much easier dihedral is an optional finish, accessible by stepping left at bolt three.
overview: Continuous friction and face moves up the smooth lens. A hard sequence leads from the gully, then a seam gives way to the rounded arete to the top, with a second hard section nearer the fourth bolt.

current.area_walk_in: Scramble up a groove-chimney under the left part of the lens, or retrace the descent gullies and traverse across to the trench beneath the route. Right Chimney is the wrong way in.
current.descent: wind eastward down gullies and slab
current.location: in a gully by the lowest part of the lens; the base is gained by a 5.5 chimney-groove under its left half

name: Meltdown
beta:
Start on Short Circuit and reach the treed ledge and belay. The second pitch ascends a slim crack that leads into the lightning-shaped feature, where only three old bolts, far apart, offer protection; the crux is here and a fall would be serious.

A shorter, easier final pitch gains the top.
overview: A serious and handsome line that follows the pale lightning-shaped vein up a hair-thin crack. The second pitch is the hard one and ends at an overlap; a shorter, easier lead then reaches the top.

current.location: shares the opening of Short Circuit, starting from the ledge that holds a tree

name: Living in America
beta: Stick-clip the first couple of bolts. Entering from the crack gives the easier start; going direct to the first clip is much harder. Six bolts lead to the anchors.

current.area_walk_in: Walk down the dirt road into The Bank, take the clear trail on the right, drop into the wash, cross it and climb the far side. Follow the signs toward the wall; the trail meets its middle section.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: just right of Ripped

name: Long Dong Wall (aka Bell Tower)
beta:
Begin beneath the saddle separating the main tower from its small southern sibling. Jam a finger-to-hand crack as far as a drilled piton, then shuffle leftward on steep face holds (the hardest moves of the route) to a stance with chains. An obvious chimney with a couple of easier spots follows.

Higher, an awkward off-width leads into another chimney that ends inside the Belfry, a see-through hole. The big final chimney demands full-body stemming and bridging past two bolts and feels harder on shorter climbers. A brief tunnel finishes at the summit.
overview: Classic multi-pitch tower route: a crack and face start, a series of chimneys through the see-through Belfry, and wild bridging up the final slot.

current.descent: rap the line with four double-rope rappels
current.location: Below the notch separating the Kissing Couple from the smaller tower just south of it

name: Loose Ends
beta:
The line opens on the edge of a shallow flake that faces left, then trends up and leftward to a belay on the neighbouring buttress.

Next, tackle the leftmost of a pair of long finger cracks up to a perch on top of a flake, then a leaning dihedral reaches a large terrace. Scramble onward to the cave region and choose any finish. Bring a cam up to 3.5.
overview: A four-pitch Book classic on excellent rock: a flake, a long finger crack, a leaning corner, then easy ground to the Cave.

current.descent: Usual way down heads east over slabs, then south through deadfall; a brief third-class step lands above the Cave, then an eastward channel leads onto an airy ledge holding two big pines, then down a third-class gully that is frequently wet
current.location: Shallow flake (facing left) just right of Pear Buttress, where the trail meets the cliff

name: Lycra Bikers From Hell
beta:
Scramble a ramp to a leaning block beneath the arch's left end, then trend rightward on a thin seam past two old pins into a finger crack. Tip-jam leftward past three bolts and move delicately to the last bolt under the roof of the arch.

The roof pull is the crux. Rappel from anchors there, or add a short bolted face pitch to reach the summit.
overview: A thin seam past old pins into a bolted tips crack, then over the arch roof to the Flight for Life anchor.

current.descent: rap 80 ft to the ground
current.location: From the big leaning block where the ramp ends under the arch’s left end

name: Golddigger's Corner
beta: Work cracks inside a corner that faces right using finger and hand jams plus stemming, arriving at the first belay ledge of the neighbouring Honey Pot route. Then rappel down to the broad terrace.
overview: Cracks in a corner that faces right, climbed by jamming hands and fingers plus stemming, leading up to the lower belay ledge of Honey Pot.

current.descent: 130 ft rappel down to the ledge you started from
current.location: reaches the first belay ledge of Honey Pot

name: Undecided
beta:
Pitch one is an easy ramp scramble, up and to the left, to a stance beneath the corner. Pitch two climbs the corner briefly, crosses toward an arete on the right, and resumes up the corner to another stance.

Walk off westward via ramps and slabs, or rappel from a conifer on the west side.
overview: A good two-pitch outing up the big open book that bounds the west side of the main wall.

current.descent: scramble west around the wall on ramps and slabs, or rap 150 ft from a conifer over the low practice slabs
current.location: The big open book (facing right) at the west (left) end of the main wall; start from the high point of the talus

name: Malign
beta: Varied moves with good protection: follow a broken corner system angling rightward, staying clear on the right side of the painted peace symbol and the steeper wall, to reach an open book near the top.
overview: Varied moderate climb up a right-trending corner system that ends in an open book; protection is good.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Broken corner system angling right, keeping right of the painted peace sign

name: Mark Finds Bob Bolting
beta: A white face leads up to anchors underneath a conspicuous horizontal break. Five bolts protect it, and a few clips are awkward.
overview: Climbs the pale face to anchors under a conspicuous horizontal crack; a few of the clips are awkward.

current.area_walk_in: Walk the dirt road for roughly half a mile, then take the trail that heads left and switchbacks up to the base of the cliff.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Lubrication
beta:
Friction up a gorgeous slab, clipping two bolts, to a tree belay. Then slant along the sloping, water-streaked groove toward a slick bulge, where protection is poor, and carry on to a comfortable terrace.

A runout, easier variation uses the slab below the groove, and a rightward traverse is possible to join Direct. Above the terrace, cross two bands of roof.
overview: Friction up a lovely slab past a pair of bolts to a tree belay, then angle along a tilted water-streak groove to a slick bulge and a good ledge, with roof bands to finish.

current.area_walk_in: Find a clear footpath climbing the grassy slope to the north, passing just east of two water tanks. After about 100 yards a fainter trail forks left at a cairn; follow it northwest up the steep hillside to the base of the wall, near the route Up. To reach Lubrication and the routes to its right, branch off to the right sooner.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Men at Work
beta: One long pitch beginning midway up the slanting flake beneath Borghoff's Blunder. Trend rightward to a dynamic move that forms the crux, then keep going past pockets and further hard bits. Fixed pitons protect the line; carry two ropes for the descent.
overview: A long single pitch that moves rightward to a dynamic crux, then keeps working through potholes and further hard sections.

current.descent: two-rope rappel from the anchors
current.location: starts midway along the slanting flake/crack beneath Borghoff's Blunder

name: Mes Amis
beta: Get over a bulging prow, then clip bolts up the smooth, bald slab toward an anchor in the upper left corner, nine clips altogether.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.anchor: bolt anchor at the upper left
current.location: crosses a prow low down, then a smooth slab

name: Queasy Street
beta: Pitch one is free climbing to a ledge belay. Pitch two mixes free and aid up the crescent arch to a hanging sling belay, and the third hooks out and follows seams. Thin aid gear, RPs and hooks are the tools; descend by rappel.
overview: An aid line beneath a crescent-shaped arch. After a free section to a ledge, the next lead mixes free and aid moves along the arch toward a sling belay, and a final stretch hooks out of it and follows seams.

current.descent: rappel the route
current.detailed_rack: a generous supply of delicate aid pieces including bird beaks, crack'n ups, RPs plus hooks; a hammer is of little use
current.location: on the wall adjacent to the Golden Waves line, starting under the crescent-moon-shaped arch

name: Mission Accomplished
beta: Begin on Mission Impossible, but keep going straight up the thin dihedral rather than angling away, and tie into Fascist Drill by its last bolt. Protection is sparse, so RPs are worth carrying.
overview: A poorly protected thin corner that branches off Mission Impossible and links into Fascist Drill.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Monkey Gone to Heaven
beta: Start beside a dead snag under a white dike, then climb directly up the steepening face to the ledge with its single bolt, continuing on bolts above.
overview: A steepening wall climbed straight up from a white dike, with a good ledge about a third of the way.

current.descent: rappel with one rope
current.location: starts at a dead tree under a pale dike on the wall

name: Morrocan Roll
beta: The opening moves to the first bolt are runout, so be ready for it; four bolts then lead to the anchors.
overview: Scales the north side of a featureless arete on a big pillar standing apart from the main wall.

current.area_walk_in: Cross Sand Gulch on the trail that climbs into the Gallery canyon, then keep to the right branch at the Mural Wall fork; it ends right at the cliff.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: north-side arete of a large pillar, south of the main wall

name: Mr. Gone
beta:
Pitch one is thin face moves past three bolts that ease into an excellent finger crack in a steep slab. The short second pitch crosses an easy slab with nothing to clip, ending at the prow's foot.

Pitch three climbs the prow itself to a bolt; trend right for easier cracks or stay on the line and reach a bolted perch beside a stepped band of roofs. The last pitch stems an easy big dihedral to the top.
overview: A four-pitch line across the face's mid-section below a conspicuous prow, mixing thin face climbing, a fine finger crack and a dihedral finish to the top.

current.area_walk_in: Follow the Summit trail until it runs along the base of the wall, then leave it and scramble uphill in the forest until you reach the face.
current.descent: two rappels (100 ft, then 150 ft) from the mid-wall stance, or walk off from the top
current.location: middle of the wall under a conspicuous prow

name: Musical Partners
beta:
Start by slanting up left across a slab to a broken finger crack, then continue onto a slender, elongated shelf. The second pitch is a sustained crack taking fingers then hands, the best of the route.

Higher, a chimney leads into an awkward, hard-to-protect slot, and the exit works left on runout face with some poor rock. Broken, bushy ground follows before the line joins a neighbouring route's groove.
overview: A seven-pitch outing up the leftmost crack line on the higher eastern wall, from the gully bottom to the rim. Pitch two is a long, continuous finger-to-hand crack of high quality.

current.area_walk_in: Almost everyone descends Cruise Gully, entered at a sign on the rim between the campground and the ranger station. It steps down through two rappel sections, often with fixed lines already in place, and lets out on bushy talus at the foot of the wall.
current.location: Under the second crack line over from Leisure Climb, at the very left of the grass shelf.

name: New Era
beta: Follow the big obvious dihedral in two or three pitches. The hard part is a layback directly under the top belay ledge. Medium to large gear supplements the few existing pins.
overview: Well-loved line up the big, obvious corner, done in two or three pitches; the hardest move is a layback shortly before the top belay.

current.area_walk_in: Walk uphill on the established trails toward the face; the long dihedral on the face makes an easy landmark to aim for.
current.descent: downclimb the south side from the summit
current.location: in the large, obvious dihedral on the rock's eastern side

name: Night Vision
beta: Clip the bolts as directionals when toproping, which keeps you from taking a long swing.

current.area_walk_in: Cross Boulder Creek from the highway, then climb the short trail to the base. Most Boulder Canyon crags are within about 5 to 15 minutes of the road.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Left-hand edge of the little block below Cob Rock's northern wall

name: Nobody Here But Us Chickens
beta: A short dihedral leaning left gets you to a desperate slab above; finish by stepping right to the anchor.
overview: A brief corner leads onto a very thin slab, a testing little pitch that ends at paired bolts beside a small tree.

current.area_walk_in: A path drops into the gulch and climbs out the far side to the base of the wall.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: North Face
beta: Traverse an exposed ridge to reach the pinnacle's steep north side, finishing on an easy slab. Much of it is sideways movement and reversing moves, so carry slings for prusiks.
overview: The historic line up the Flatirons' most dramatic spire: it wanders along an exposed ridge, crosses onto the steep north wall and finishes on an easy slab. Much of it traverses or goes down, so a fall can leave a climber hanging off route; plenty of old fixed pins.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Not Long For This World
beta: Usually toproped. Step into the shallow corner facing right on the dihedral's northern side; wired nuts and small cams are what the line takes.
overview: Usually toproped. It sits on the northern wall of a big, wide-open dihedral and climbs into a shallow corner whose face points right.

current.area_walk_in: A brief, steep, eroded track fords the creek and ascends the slope to the wall's foot. Numbering runs north to south; to find route one, start at the Buoux Block and head north.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: south of the other routes, beyond a pine tree, within a big open-book dihedral

name: Pessimismus
beta:
Share the opening lead with Topnotch, then keep following the corner system to a ledge under a giant gaping flake. Next, angle left and upward into a grey open-book that faces right, ending on a bolted stance.

The crux is the steep face above with two bolts, reaching a seam that tops out The Shield; a leaning flake-crack finishes it.
overview: A sustained route through The Shield's right part. After Topnotch's opening lead, a corner and a big flake give way to a grey dihedral, a bolted face crux and a final flake-crack leaning leftward that finishes as Topnotch does.

current.location: through the right part of The Shield, beginning with Topnotch's opening lead

name: Nuclear Polka
beta:
Ascend the open book that leans left, going past the large roof near the face's right edge, which is the crux; a crack holding two pins then ends at a belay perched on a sloping stance. RPs and TCUs belong on the rack.

Higher, shift left, jam a crack about two inches wide and exit rightward.
overview: The dihedral beside the big roof holds the crux, then a crack with a pair of fixed pins leads to a sloping belay. The final stretch shifts left for a crack about two inches wide and finishes rightward.

current.area_walk_in: A path drops into the gulch and climbs out the far side to the base of the wall.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Obscura Direct
beta:
The first lead is a simple hand-width crack to a tiny stance under an upper corner. The second edges up that narrow corner on a thin crack, steps left onto an unprotected slab, and goes over the arch.

A selection of nuts and one large cam protect the arch moves.
overview: Two pitches on steep slab: a moderate jam crack, then a slim right-facing corner and a run-out slab step to surmount the big arch.

current.area_walk_in: Several short, steep trails climb the slope to the base of the crag.
current.detailed_rack: A set of nuts plus a big cam to guard the moves over the arch.
current.location: From a ledge to Tilted Tower's right, starting up a moderate hand crack

name: One for the Road
beta: Start on the face to the east of Twin Cracks and follow broken seams past four bolts to a lowering anchor. A #2 cam covers the runout before the first bolt.
overview: Discontinuous cracks on the face beside Twin Cracks, bolted to a chained lower-off; a cam protects the runout before the first bolt.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: on the face just right of Twin Cracks

name: Ophir Broke
beta: A hard, overhanging crack on the east flank of the wall. Carry two full sets of cams; it also goes as an easy aid line.
overview: A strenuous overhanging hand crack on the Mirror Wall's eastern part, among the state's first 5.12s; also a fine clean-aid line.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: The Mirror Wall's eastern part

name: Optic Nerve
beta: Start by a small tree with a brief finger crack, angle up rightward onto a flake, after which smear directly up the slab to finish.
overview: A brief finger crack and flake, then unprotected friction to the top; usually best on toprope.

current.area_walk_in: Scramble up a groove-chimney under the left part of the lens, or retrace the descent gullies and traverse across to the trench beneath the route. Right Chimney is the wrong way in.
current.descent: descend a simple gully on the north, then walk round to the base
current.location: About 50 ft down and left of The Frame, by a small tree above Ellipse

name: Optical Illusions
beta:
Face climb up and rightward past six bolts, with the hardest move right before the final one, then work left onto a ledge and belay.

Above, three bolts lead into a finger-width crack; jam it to the top ledge. TCUs and small cams help there.
overview: Two pitches: a bolted face to a ledge, then more bolts into a finger crack.

current.descent: rappel 23 m to the ground
current.location: just east of the block at the base

name: Original Sin
beta: Climb the large corner system leaning right in the wall's bottom right and descend by rappelling from a tree.

current.descent: rappel off a tree
current.location: big right-facing dihedral that leans, at the lower right of the wall
